calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if a deadline is < 90 days from 2026-11-13, otherwise High/Medium/Low by importance), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

items.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride
items.reason: FDA final order removes methylene chloride, ethylene dichloride and trichloroethylene as extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin and turmeric oleoresin. These are common natural colors in meat and candy. Industry has reportedly abandoned these uses, so real impact is probably low. The order takes effect 2027-01-11.
items.action: Ask color suppliers to confirm in writing that annatto, paprika and turmeric colorants used in hot dogs, casings and gummies are made without these solvents. File any objections by 2026-12-12. Update specs before 2027-01-11.

items.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
items.reason: FDA final order revokes methylene chloride as a diluent in inks used to mark fruit and vegetables, on Delaney Clause grounds. This could touch apple marking inks on our supply. The petition's other requests were denied as moot. The order takes effect 2027-01-11.
items.action: Confirm with apple suppliers and packers that no methylene-chloride-based marking inks are used on apples we buy. Add this to supplier specs before 2027-01-11. Note the 2026-12-12 objection date.

items.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
items.reason: USDA proposes to narrow which TANF benefits automatically qualify a household for SNAP. USDA estimates about 16.9% of participating households would lose benefits. That would cut SNAP-funded purchases at our grocery and convenience customers.
items.action: Model the SNAP sales exposure by customer and channel. Decide whether to file comments, directly or through a trade association, by 2026-12-10. Brief customers' category managers.

items.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
items.reason: USDA proposes to codify the One Big Beautiful Bill Act changes to the SNAP three-month time limit. It would change the exceptions, tighten waiver rules and revise the definition of a homeless individual. That could reduce the number of SNAP shoppers and our SNAP-driven demand.
items.action: Estimate the volume at risk in SNAP-heavy stores and fold it into demand forecasts. Decide whether to comment by 2026-12-10. Monitor state implementation.

items.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
items.reason: AMS proposes changes to the pecan marketing order (Order 986). It would change sheller membership and nominations and the inter-handler transfer report form. It would also add late fees and interest on unpaid assessments. This affects pecan handlers and could affect our pecan supply chain and costs.
items.action: Check whether Brightside or its pecan suppliers act as handlers under the order. Talk to shellers about assessment and reporting impacts. Decide whether to comment by 2026-12-09.

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — Brightside Foods Co.
Window 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-13 · as of 2026-11-13 · 5 items

## Critical (5)

- **Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride** [web search — verify]
  - Ask color suppliers to confirm in writing that annatto, paprika and turmeric colorants used in hot dogs, casings and gummies are made without these solvents. File any objections by 2026-12-12. Update specs before 2027-01-11.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-12 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory) · Areas: food-safety
  - 91 FR 72410 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22866/color-additive-petition-from-the-international-association-of-color-manufacturers-request-to-amend
- **Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene** [web search — verify]
  - Confirm with apple suppliers and packers that no methylene-chloride-based marking inks are used on apples we buy. Add this to supplier specs before 2027-01-11. Note the 2026-12-12 objection date.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-12 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory) · Areas: food-safety
  - 91 FR 72413 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22865/color-additive-petition-from-environmental-defense-fund-et-al-request-to-amend-the-color-additive
- **Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility** [web search — verify]
  - Model the SNAP sales exposure by customer and channel. Decide whether to file comments, directly or through a trade association, by 2026-12-10. Brief customers' category managers.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-10 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance) · Areas: sales
  - 91 FR 72454 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22936/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-reforming-categorical-eligibility
- **Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults** [web search — verify]
  - Estimate the volume at risk in SNAP-heavy stores and fold it into demand forecasts. Decide whether to comment by 2026-12-10. Monitor state implementation.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-10 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance) · Areas: sales
  - 91 FR 72439 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22944/modification-to-work-requirements-for-able-bodied-adults
- **Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements** [web search — verify]
  - Check whether Brightside or its pecan suppliers act as handlers under the order. Talk to shellers about assessment and reporting impacts. Decide whether to comment by 2026-12-09.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-09 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Tom Alvarez (Sourcing) · Areas: sourcing
  - 91 FR 70809 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22826/pecans-grown-in-the-states-of-alabama-arkansas-arizona-california-florida-georgia-kansas-louisiana

perItem.why: Plain-English reason naming meat, casings and gummies. Concrete steps: get written supplier confirmation, file objections by 2026-12-12, update specs before 2027-01-11. Sales owner fits the topic. Hedged on impact ('probably low').
Concrete steps on apple suppliers and marking inks, with a deadline and a spec update. The 'Delaney Clause' jargon is explained only partly. The objection-date step ('note the date') is vague.

Clear exposure estimate (16.9% of households) tied to grocery and convenience customers, with concrete modeling and a comment decision. 'Categorical eligibility' and 'TANF' are jargon. Owner fits customer-facing compliance.
Concrete step to estimate volume at risk and fold it into forecasts. 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' and 'three-month time limit' need translation. 'Monitor state implementation' is generic.

Concrete check on whether Brightside acts as a handler, with a comment deadline. 'Marketing order,' 'sheller,' and 'inter-handler transfer report' are jargon. Sourcing owner fits, but the supply impact is only speculative.
